LESSON: INTRODUCTION TO SPACE PHYSICS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS
Strand: Environmental and Space Physics
Topic 4.2: Introduction to Space Physics
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Introduction to Space Physics, part of Environmental and Space Physics in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS.

Key inquiry question: How was the universe / earth formed? 2. How do we benefit from Astrophysics?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss in groups the big bang theory on the origin of the universe (Big bang theory) and make notes. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Introduction to Space Physics together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: the learner develops the skill of interacting with digital technology. They use digital technology to

accomplish their own tasks to search for information and media on methods of space exploration and planetary motion.

Values to be developed

● Integrity: the learner demonstrates fairness as they utilize the available resources prudently while modeling the

planetary motion.

● Love: the learner demonstrates self-sacrifice by putting the interest of others before their own as they use digital

media to observe the celestial bodies, methods of space exploration and planetary motion.
